documentNotes.title: Instructions
documentNotes.statement:
This test has 40 questions.

Look at every page and read the questions carefully.

You have 45 minutes to complete the test. If you finish early wait silently until the 45 minutes are over.

Each question is multiple-choice. Choose A, B, C or D. Only one answer is correct.

Some questions contain a short video clip (indicated with [film-reel icon]). Click inside the video frame to start it.

Mark your choice on the Answer Sheet by making a circle around the letter that you want to select. If you make a mistake cross out the selected letter and circle a new choice.

For navigation it is best to use the arrows on the keyboard to move to the next (↓ →) or previous (↑ ←) page. DO NOT CLICK ON THE ESCAPE BUTTON, AS THAT ENDS THE PRESENTATION.

Good luck!

documentNotes.title: THE END
documentNotes.statement:
You have reached the last slide of the Multimedia Test.

Click on the arrow ↑ or ← to go back to the previous page(s) if you want to check your answers

OR

wait silently until the time is over.

problems.title: Q.1
problems.statement:
Pingualuit, the Canadian lake in the middle of the satellite image, was formed through which process?

A. meteorite impact

B. glacial erosion

C. permafrost melting

D. volcanic eruption

figures.alt: Satellite image of a tundra landscape with many irregular dark lakes; in the middle a perfectly circular dark-blue lake surrounded by a raised light rim. Scale bar 1 km and a north arrow in the lower right corner.

problems.title: Q.2
problems.statement:
According to this map, which of the following groups of countries can be considered most at risk from the effects of climate change?

A. Afghanistan, Chad and Guatemala

B. Botswana, Peru and Saudi Arabia

C. Cuba, Malaysia and South Korea

D. Italy, Spain and Uruguay

figures.alt: World map of countries coloured by a climate-change vulnerability score, with a legend from 'most at risk' to 'least at risk': 30-39 (dark red), 40-49 (red-orange), 50-59 (orange), 60-69 (light green), 70-79 (green), 80+ (dark green). Labelled countries: USA, Canada, Greenland, Mexico, Brazil, Russia, Kazakhstan, Mongolia, China, India, Australia. Much of Africa and South Asia is dark red or red.

problems.title: Q.3
problems.statement:
Which natural phenomenon most likely caused the destruction shown in the picture?

A. earthquake

B. hurricane

C. mudslide

D. tornado

figures.alt: Photo of a street of small single-storey houses after a disaster: cars stand upended vertically against the house walls, debris lies on the wet street and people stand in front of the houses. 'REUTERS' credit in the lower right corner.

problems.title: Q.4
problems.statement:
The amount of energy produced by a hydropower plant is mainly determined by:

A. the elevation distance the water falls

B. the volume of the water flow

C. both the volume and the elevation distance

D. the distance the transmission lines travel from the plant

figures.alt: Cross-section diagram of a hydropower dam in a green mountain valley, with labels: transmission lines, Dam, Penstock, Generators, Turbines, and 'Cross section of hydropower facility'. Water from the reservoir on the right flows down the penstock through the dam to the turbines and out into the river on the left; pylons carry the transmission lines.

problems.title: Q.5
problems.statement:
The valley in the picture below was formed by:

A. a fault

B. a flash flood

C. a glacier

D. a lava flow

figures.alt: Photo of a broad green mountain valley with steep grassy slopes on both sides and a wide flat floor along which a braided stream flows towards the viewer; clouds cover the ridges.

problems.title: Q.6
problems.statement:
What caused the red colouring in this sandstone?

A. calcium carbonate

B. copper sulphate

C. iron oxide

D. organic matter

figures.alt: Close-up photo of a sandstone surface streaked in red and white, with a hiker's shoe and shadow in the lower part and gravel in the upper left corner.

problems.title: Q.7
problems.statement:
The map shows regions which are major producers of:

A. apples

B. bananas

C. citrus

D. cotton

figures.alt: World map (elliptical projection) with green-to-black shading of production areas: the south-eastern USA, north-eastern Brazil, the West African Sahel, Central Asia, Pakistan and north-western India, eastern China and eastern Australia. Colour scale 50, 100, 150, 200 labelled 'Average regional output (kg/ha)'.

problems.title: Q.8
problems.statement:
The figure represents the distribution among continents of:

B. mining industry

C. population

figures.alt: Grey world map with bar charts per continent for the years 1800, 1900, 2000 and 2050 (legend 'YEAR'). North America: 0.7%, 5.0%, 5.1%, 4.4%. Latin America: 2.5%, 4.5%, 8.6%, 9.1%. Europe: 20.8%, 24.7%, 12.0%, 7.0%. Africa: 10.9%, 8.1%, 12.9%, 19.8%. Asia: 64.9%, 57.4%, 60.8%, 59.1%. Oceania: 0.2%, 0.4%, 0.5%, 0.5%.

Occurrences like this are most likely to happen when structures are built on which type of ground surface?

problems.title: Q.10

problems.title: Q.11
problems.statement: The figure at the bottom is a diagrammatic representation of a town plan. Considering the prevailing wind over the year, in which zone (A, B, C or D) would you locate a high-class residential area?

figures.alt: Top: two wind roses, 'January' (blue, winds mainly from the west and south-west) and 'July' (red, winds mainly from the south-west), with compass directions N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW and rings 0 to 12%. Bottom: town plan with zones A (west), B (centre), C (east) and D (south-east), a green 'Heavy Manufacturing' block north of zone B's western part, and a north arrow.

problems.title: Q.12

The altimeter in the photograph indicates metres. Where was the picture taken?

B. Lake Lugano

problems.title: Q.13
problems.statement:
Which of these statements is supported by the evidence in the graph?

A. About 94% of all South Asian tourists did not travel to Country X.

B. About half the tourists travelling to Country X came from East Asia.

C. African tourists like travelling to Country Y more than to Country X.

D. In 2011, the number of European tourists dropped.

figures.alt: Horizontal bar chart 'Tourist Arrivals in Country X by Origin, 2010 and 2011' in percent (axis 0.00 to 60.00 %), light bars 2010 and dark bars 2011: Africa 0.78 / 0.72; Middle East 3.70 / 3.29; Oceania 5.00 / 4.86; South Asia 6.28 / 6.21; The Americas 5.32 / 4.96; Europe 27.36 / 25.65; East Asia 51.55 / 54.31.

problems.title: Q.14

What is the main income source of this person?

A. cultivating

B. fishing

C. herding

D. mining

figures.alt: Photo of a young person in a dark-red robe with an orange sash assembling the wooden lattice frame of a yurt in falling snow; a yak and other people in the background.

problems.title: Q.15
problems.statement:
The phenomenon shown in this video is caused by:

A. heating of greenhouse gasses by sunlight

B. ionization by the solar wind of $\mathrm{O_2}$ and $\mathrm{N_2}$ in the thermosphere

C. reflection of sunlight by aerosols of volcanic origin

D. refraction of sunlight by ice crystals in the stratosphere

answer.note: The video clip is not contained in the PDF; the slide shows only an empty video frame.

problems.title: Q.16
problems.statement:
Lines 1 to 4 in the graph correspond to different latitudes. Which one of the following statements is correct?

A. All latitudes shown in this graph are in the southern hemisphere.

B. At latitude 1, the Sun is perpendicular to the Earth’s surface at solar noon at the June solstice.

C. Latitude 3 is closer to the equator than latitude 2.

D. Latitude 4 is closer to a polar circle than latitude 1.

figures.alt: Line graph 'Monthly values of solar radiation': Insolation (Wm⁻²) from 0 to 600 against Month J to D, with dashed vertical lines at the March Equinox, June Solstice, September Equinox and December Solstice. Line 1 (yellow) is 0 until the March equinox, peaks at about 510 at the June solstice and returns to 0 at the September equinox; line 2 (red) goes from about 25 in January to about 470 in June and back to about 25 in December; line 3 (green) varies from about 230 to about 480 with its maximum in June; line 4 (blue) stays between about 385 (June) and about 430 (equinoxes).

problems.title: Q.17
problems.statement: In which climatic region (A, B, C or D) would tropical rainforests be found?

figures.alt: Four climate charts (monthly precipitation bars in mm and temperature line in °C, months 01 to 12). A: Altitude 18m, °C 12.4, mm 592. B: Altitude 39m, °C 22.6, mm 157, no rain from June to September. C: Altitude 21m, °C 27.2, mm 2101, temperature almost constant near 27 °C and heavy rain all year. D: Altitude 186m, °C 9.9, mm 623, temperature from about 0 °C in January to 20 °C in July.

problems.title: Q.18
problems.statement:
The coloured areas in the 3D model represent places that:

A. are at greatest risk of avalanches

B. are at greatest risk of earthquakes

C. receive the highest rainfall in winter

D. receive more solar radiation in summer

figures.alt: 3D terrain model of a mountain area drawn with contour lines (height axis 0 to 1000, coordinate axes 8676000 to 8684000 and 509000 to 515000); the steepest slopes are coloured red and purple according to a legend 'Slope (deg.)' from 0 to 60, the coloured classes covering about 28 to 44 degrees.

problems.title: Q.19
problems.statement:
What process does the illustration represent?

A. forest degradation

B. risk in forest ecosystems

C. forest succession

D. the geographical zonation of plants

figures.alt: Illustration with a legend 1 Bare Rock, 2 Mosses Grasses, 3 Grasses Perennials, 4 Woody Pioneers, 5 Fast Growing Trees, 6 Climax Forest; curves 1 to 6 rise and fall one after another along a 'Time' arrow. Below, six soil blocks with increasingly tall vegetation from bare rock to a dense forest, arrows from a 'Disturbance' bar with fire, human, flood and biohazard icons, and at the bottom a rising curve 'Increase over Time: Biodiversity, Biomass, Soil Layer'.

problems.title: Q.20
problems.statement:
According to the current global value chain, Nutella® would stop production without input from which of these countries:

A. Colombia

B. Germany

C. Malaysia

D. South Africa

figures.alt: World map 'The Nutella® global value chain. Source: Ferrero, Sourcemap and various on-line sources.' Legend: Headquarters (blue hexagon, Ferrero Group Alba, Italy), Main international suppliers (green circles: France (vanillin & sugar), Turkey (hazelnut), Nigeria (cocoa), Malaysia (palm oil), Brazil (sugar)), Factories (red triangles: Brantford, Canada; Villers-Ecalles, France; Stadtallendorf, Germany; Belsk, Poland; Vladimir, Russia; Alba and Sant'Angelo dei Lombardi, Italy; Poços de Caldas, Brazil; Los Cardales, Argentina; Lithgow, Australia) and Main sales offices (purple crosses, among them one in South Africa).

This time-series of photos was taken in which country?

A. Chile

C. Norway

figures.alt: Composite of 13 vertical photo strips of the sun over the sea next to a dark cliff; from left to right the sun sinks towards the horizon and rises again without setting, and a clock face under each strip shows the hour.

problems.title: Q.22
problems.statement:
Which of these statements is best supported by the evidence in the graphs?

A. City 1 has a higher rate of emigration than City 2.

B. City 2 has a higher rate of emigration than City 1.

C. These two cities have no emigration.

D. Both cities have the same rate of emigration.

figures.alt: Two population pyramids side by side, 'City 1' (left, pink background) and 'City 2' (right, grey background), each with Male (blue, right) and Female (red, left) bars for the age groups 0-4 to 95-99 and '100 and more'. City 1 has a broad base narrowing steadily upwards; City 2 has a narrow base, a pronounced notch in the 30-34 and 35-39 groups and its widest bars at ages 50-59 and 70-74.

problems.title: Q.23
problems.statement:
Which of the following statements is correct?

A. Chile and Vietnam have the same number of Internet users.

B. The number of Internet users in Germany is larger than in Canada.

C. Chinese Internet users are a greater proportion of their population than Spanish Internet users are of theirs.

D. The number of Internet users in India is smaller than in Italy.

figures.alt: Cartogram 'Internet Penetration': each country is a rectangle whose area is proportional to its total number of Internet users (legend squares 100, 50 and 10 million) and whose shade of red shows Internet penetration in % of population (Under 20%, 20% - 40%, 41% - 50%, 51% - 60%, Over 60%). Large rectangles for United States, China and Japan; labelled countries include Canada, United Kingdom, Germany, France, Spain, Italy, Russia, Poland, Turkey, Iran, India, Brazil, MEX, COL, VEN, CHL, ARG, VNM, THA, Indonesia, Australia and others. Small unreadable credits text in the lower right.

problems.title: Q.24
problems.statement:
In which watershed are these rivers, with their marked colour difference, located?

A. Amazon River Basin

B. Mississippi River Basin

C. Nile River Basin

D. Yellow River Basin

figures.alt: Aerial photo of dense green tropical forest: a wide brown, sediment-laden river runs across the image and a narrower green-coloured river joins it from below, the two waters meeting with a sharp colour boundary; a small clearing with buildings on the right bank of the tributary.

problems.title: Q.25
problems.statement:
In this classic model, the area labelled 5 corresponds to Asian cities. Area 4 represents the cities of which location?

figures.alt: Scatter plot 'Urban density and transport-related energy consumption in 50 cities (Newman and Kenworthy, 1989)': Annual energy consumption per inhabitant (MJ), 0 to 90000, against Urban density (inhabitant per ha), 0 to 300, with a red decreasing curve. Five groups of points are circled and numbered: 1 (light blue, density about 10-25, 50000-77000 MJ), 2 (red, density about 20-45, 33000-47000 MJ), 3 (black, density about 10-20, 35000-45000 MJ), 4 (dark blue, density about 30-75, 18000-29000 MJ) and 5 (green, density about 70-300, 5000-18000 MJ).

problems.title: Q.26
problems.statement:

A. annual precipitation

figures.alt: World choropleth map with a legend of coloured triangles along the top: 50M+, 20-50+, 10-20M, 5-10M, 2-5M, 1-2M, 500K-1M, 100-500K, 50K-100K, under 50K and No data. The USA and China are in the 50M+ class, Russia, Mexico and several European countries in 20-50+, Canada and Saudi Arabia in 10-20M; much of Africa and Central Asia has no data.

Which country does the graph correspond to?

problems.title: Q.28
problems.statement:
What natural phenomena do these graphs refer to?

A. forest fires

B. hydro-meteorological

C. tsunamis

D. volcanic eruptions

figures.alt: Graph 'Historical fatalities': Cumulative fatalities (thousands), 0 to 300, from 1600 to 2000. Line 1 'Total from all 533 fatal incidents' rises in steps annotated '1792 14,524 fatalities', '1815 60,000 fatalities', '1883 36,417 fatalities', '1902 28,800 fatalities' and '1985 23,187 fatalities', reaching about 280; line 2 'Total with 5 biggest incidents removed' reaches about 115 and line 3 'Total with 10 biggest incidents removed' about 80. Below, a bar 'Current risk:' divided into Indonesia 66%, Philippines 10.6%, Japan 6.9%, Mexico 3.9%, Ethiopia 3.9% and Other 8.7%.

problems.title: Q.29
problems.statement:
The Sustainable Society Index (SSI) shows at a glance the level of sustainability of a given region, based on 21 indicators. Which country does the SSI shown in the graph correspond to?

A. Costa Rica

B. Libya

C. Norway

D. Vietnam

figures.alt: Radar chart with 21 axes grouped under Human Wellbeing (Sufficient Food, Sufficient to Drink, Safe Sanitation, Education, Healthy Life, Gender Equality, Income Distribution, Population Growth, Good Governance), Environmental Wellbeing (Biodiversity, Renewable Water Resources, Consumption, Energy Use, Energy Savings, Greenhouse Gases, Renewable Energy, Organic Farming) and Economic Wellbeing (Genuine Savings, GDP, Employment, Public Debt). The green area reaches the outer ring for Sufficient Food, Public Debt and Education, is high for the other human-wellbeing indicators and Greenhouse Gases, and is very small for Organic Farming, Renewable Energy, Renewable Water Resources, Biodiversity and Energy Use.

problems.title: Q.30
problems.statement:
In which country would you find this landscape?

A. Panama

B. Peru

C. Spain

D. Uruguay

figures.alt: Block diagram of a snow-capped mountain rising from sea level, with altitudinal zones TIERRA CALIENTE, TIERRA TEMPLADA (above 3,000 ft. (900 m)), TIERRA FRÍA (above 6,000 ft. (1,800 m)), TIERRA HELADA (above 12,000 ft. (3,600 m)) and the Snowline at 15,000 ft. (4,600 m). In which country were these photos taken?

A. Egypt

problems.title: Q.37
problems.statement:
The image shows:

A. dispersion in the atmosphere of volcanic ash

B. flow of electricity due to a lightning discharge

C. area affected by a tropical cyclone

problems.title: Q.38
problems.statement:
Which statement about the qanat system, traditionally used in areas of West Asia, is incorrect?

A. It can only draw sustainable amounts from the aquifer.

B. It is energy efficient, using gravity to transport water.

C. It uses readily available surface water.

D. Its underground channels minimise evaporation.

figures.alt: Cross-section 'Diagram of a qanat system': a gently sloping underground channel runs from the Mother Well ('The main water source for the qanat'), which reaches below the Water Table, through a series of vertical Access Shafts ('Permits access to the qanat channel for construction and maintenance'), along the Qanat Channel ('The qanat's water-carrying channel') to an Outlet and a Distribution area ('A network of dams, gates and channels is used to distribute the water') on Irrigated Land. Layers of Alluvium over Bedrock.

problems.title: Q.39
problems.statement: This world map by Arabian cartographer Muhammad al-Idrisi was the most accurate cartographic depiction of the world when it was made in 1154. Which letter (A, B, C or D) marks the Mediterranean Sea?

figures.alt: Reproduction of al-Idrisi's world map (yellow land, dark blue seas, oriented with south at the top), with climate numbers X. to I. along the top edge and four circled letters on water bodies: A near the upper left, B on an enclosed sea in the lower middle, C on the large sea in the right half, D on the sea at the lower right.

problems.title: Q.40
problems.statement:
The photo was taken at the point marked on Lac Leman (Lake Geneva) in September 2014. In which direction was the camera pointing and what was the time of day?

A. towards Lausanne, early morning

B. towards Lausanne, midday

C. towards Montreux, early morning

D. towards Montreux, midday

figures.alt: Photo of terraced vineyards on a steep slope above a lake, with a road and a railway along the shore and mountains in the distance; the vine rows cast only short shadows.

Google map of the eastern part of Lake Geneva with Lausanne, Pully, Lutry, Cully, Chexbres, Chardonne, Corsier-sur-Vevey, Vevey, La Tour-de-Peilz, Montreux, Veytaux and Villeneuve on the north shore, Évian-les-Bains, Thollon-les-Mémises and Saint-Gingolph on the south shore, and the Schweiz/France border; a red marker on the north shore between Chexbres and Chardonne, west of Vevey.
